package.description: Keeps Windows awake only while the app you pick is actually working, then releases the lock by itself.

en-US.description: Keeps Windows awake only while the app you pick is actually working, then releases the lock by itself.
en-US.longDescription:
WakeWhile prevents Windows from sleeping while a specific application is
genuinely doing work, and lets the PC sleep again once it goes quiet.

Unlike other keep-awake tools it is not a manual toggle, so there is nothing
to remember to switch off. You pick an app from a list of your open windows
and WakeWhile watches it, and every process it has spawned, measuring CPU,
disk, network and memory once a second. Each limit is an adjustable slider
with the live reading printed underneath it.

It is a single executable of about 90 KB written in C, with no installer, no
dependencies, no background service and no administrator rights. It writes a
plain text log recording which signal kept the machine awake, so the question
of why a PC will not sleep always has an answer you can read.
en-US.name: WakeWhile
